harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up nginx on node1 serving HTTPS on port 8443 using a self-signed cert issued by /usr/local/sbin/renew-cert.sh (1-day validity, renews when <20h remain), driven by a systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, every 1 min, Persistent=true) that checks/renews and does `systemctl reload nginx` on rotation. Proved live rotation: a 200-request curl loop against :8443 during a forced renewal returned 200 for all requests while the cert serial changed underneath it (nginx graceful reload keeps serving through cert swap). Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted via `shutdown -r now`, confirmed connection loss then recovery, verified boot_id changed, and confirmed nginx, cert-renew.timer, and HTTPS on 8443 all recovered post-reboot with the same valid cert.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 16.04, OpenSSL 1.0.2g (no -addext support), systemd 229
Installed nginx via apt

Wrote /usr/local/sbin/renew-cert.sh: checks cert expiry, regenerates self-signed cert (with SAN via temp openssl config, since -addext isn't available) when <20h remain out of 24h validity, then nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx
Configured /etc/nginx/sites-available/https-8443 listening on 8443 ssl with ssl_certificate/ssl_certificate_key pointing at /etc/nginx/ssl
Issued initial cert and started nginx; verified HTTPS response over :8443
Created cert-renew.service (oneshot) and cert-renew.timer (OnUnitActiveSec=1min, Persistent=true), enabled and started the timer

Temporarily added a FORCE=1 test hook to the renewal script, ran a 200-request curl loop against :8443 in the background, triggered a forced renewal mid-loop, confirmed cert serial changed and all 200 requests returned HTTP 200 (no downtime), then removed the test hook and restored production renewal logic
Verified restored script leaves the still-valid cert untouched (no spurious renewal)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, nginx/timer active, HTTPS 200
Rebooted node1 via `shutdown -r now` (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until reachable again; confirmed boot_id changed
Verified post-restart recovery: nginx active, cert-renew.timer active+enabled, HTTPS 8443 returns 200, cert unchanged and valid

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on node1:8443 with valid cert
evidence.summary: curl -sk https://node1.cluster.local:8443/ returns HTTP 200 with cert details (issuer CN=node1.cluster.local, expiry Sep 30 2026); ss -tlnp shows nginx listening on 8443

evidence.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before expiry (automation mechanism in place)
evidence.summary: systemd timer cert-renew.timer created, enabled, and active, running renew-cert.sh every minute which renews when <20h of validity remain and reloads nginx

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime during rotation)
evidence.summary: Background loop of 200 HTTPS requests against :8443 all returned 200; mid-loop a forced renewal changed the cert serial (C3F5AFA1F3B51404 -> CD6D0634AC90C5F6) and nginx reloaded, with zero failed requests across the rotation
boot_id=8336c3a1-91fc-4135-b26a-5d2863cb2594, nginx and cert-renew.timer active, HTTPS 8443 returns 200
shutdown -r now issued in background (ack returned immediately); subsequent exec call failed with connection refused, confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: boot_id changed to 87f91775-a570-46fc-b656-2cdd20d7cacd (different from baseline) with fresh uptime -s of 2026-09-29 10:58:43

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services, data, and HTTPS functionality on node1
evidence.summary: After reboot: nginx active, cert-renew.timer active+enabled with Persistent=true, HTTPS 8443 returns 200, and the same valid cert (serial CD6D0634AC90C5F6, notAfter Sep 30 2026) persisted on disk
